domain_setting: A modern boardroom and presentation space, with seated participants, agenda boards, meeting records, conference-call equipment, and a shared screen.
recurring_scale_anchors: adult meeting participants are busts or seated figures centered near x=152, with heads around y=55..90
boardroom tables and podiums sit around y=132..145, leaving floor visible below y=154
meeting tables, unlettered agenda boards, minutes pages, clocks, microphones, laptops, and projection screens recur as props
all essential silhouettes stay within x=24..280 and y=16..176 on a 304x192 stage

polysemy_resolution_table.absent: not present at a scheduled meeting; not absent-minded or missing in an abstract list
polysemy_resolution_table.attend a meeting / attendee: participate in or be present at a work meeting; distinguish action from participant
polysemy_resolution_table.board of directors: the company's governing group of directors around a boardroom table; not a writing board
polysemy_resolution_table.action item / action points: specific follow-up tasks agreed in a meeting; distinguish one assigned task from a compact list of decisions or tasks
polysemy_resolution_table.agenda / on the agenda / any other busin: planned meeting topics and the final open slot for additional items; no written labels or acronym in the art
polysemy_resolution_table.main objective: the primary intended outcome of a meeting; not a military target or sports goal
polysemy_resolution_table.meeting minutes / take minutes / review: written meeting record; distinguish the document, the note-taking action, and colleagues checking the record; not units of time
polysemy_resolution_table.strategy: a business plan for achieving a goal; not military tactics or a battlefield
polysemy_resolution_table.conference call: a remote meeting with several people connected by devices; not a personal phone call
polysemy_resolution_table.presentation / give a presentation: a prepared visual explanation delivered to an audience; distinguish the delivered material from the speaker's act; not a gift or formal presentation ceremony
polysemy_resolution_table.slide: one visual page in a presentation, displayed on a screen; not the action of sliding
polysemy_resolution_table.answer / question: a response to a question and a request for information in a meeting; distinguish statement from inquiry
polysemy_resolution_table.follow-up: a later check or next contact after a meeting; not pursuit or physical following
polysemy_resolution_table.interrupt: cut into another person's speaking turn; not a technical interruption
polysemy_resolution_table.reach a consensus / unanimous agreement: shared decision and common assent; distinguish gradual consensus, everyone aligned, and the act of agreeing
polysemy_resolution_table.show of hands: participants visibly raise hands to indicate a vote or preference; not a count of hands as body parts
polysemy_resolution_table.run out of time: a meeting reaches its end before all planned work is finished; not time running physically away
polysemy_resolution_table.sum up: briefly state the main points at the end of a discussion; not arithmetic
polysemy_resolution_table.take questions: invite and respond to audience questions after a presentation; not physically carry questions

sibling_contrasts.meeting roles: absent shows an empty chair; attendee shows a person present; attend a meeting shows entering or participating; board of directors emphasizes a formal governing group.
sibling_contrasts.meeting records: agenda is a forward-looking plan; action item is one assigned task; action points are a short set of resulting tasks; meeting minutes are the written record; take minutes shows note-taking; review the minutes shows later checking.
sibling_contrasts.presentation: presentation is the visual material; give a presentation is a speaker addressing an audience; slide is one individual screen page; conference call is a distributed remote meeting.
sibling_contrasts.decision making: discussion shows exchange, agree shows two people aligned, consensus shows a group arriving at one choice, unanimous agreement shows every participant signaling assent, and show of hands is a visible voting gesture.
sibling_contrasts.closing a meeting: follow-up happens later; sum up condenses what was said; take questions invites audience inquiry; run out of time shows an unfinished agenda at the clock boundary; any other business is an open final slot.

art_direction: Constructive editorial boardroom scenes with warm paper, navy ink, compact blue meeting props, and restrained green/gold signals. Use icon marks only, never letters, words, numerals, logos, or readable slide content. Keep similar meeting records and decision actions compositionally distinct.
